title: Learning music: method books, a white teacher and Hippolyte Charles's band
summary: Self-taught, with method books and chord charts from a bass teacher; he learned to read from Joe Welsh and Louis Cantrell in Hippolyte Charles's band.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Well, I was gonna ask some more about your teachers. If you're on your guitar, have you started that? Did you have a teacher or take lessons?
No, I just took it up myself. Never had no teacher at all. I just took it up myself.
Did you get a book or anything to help or just...

I did. I did get... method books from Wehrlein, you know, and sent off away and got me a good method, you see. That... I practically had a chord method. They had a... they had method with all the line of... the whole chord system, you see. And that's where I caught a whole lot of that from. But...
Did you have a teacher when you took up any bass or anything or pick that up then?

Well, I did have a teacher, a white fella. He gave me a whole lot of ideas on the fingerboard of the instrument. That was a fella called Matil Fertranger. Matil Fertranger. He had a place of business right here at Cornel and Claiborne. He was crippled. And he played at the... at the Orphan Theater. And he gave it up. But he was a good musician. So he gave me the fingerboard. You know, I used to bum around these places, see. And he'd take my liking to me. So he just gave me that fingerboard of the bass and gave me the... wrote the whole chord system for me. Oh, yeah. From the nut down. Yeah. And I just kept that, you know, and I'd study that, you know. Then I got sorted out by having friends like all these... like Mario Mineta and different good musicians, you know, one day when I'd taken up the note music, you see. They gave me ideas about the division. I practically learned the notes myself. The treble and bass. I took up both clefs at the same time. Treble and bass clefs. And that was pretty hard. Yeah. And after I learned the notes, you see, the hardest thing was dividing the notes. Division is the hardest thing in music. And after I got so well, I could... I learned the division. I was with Hippolyte Charles. I had a whole lot of help there within Hippolyte Charles' band because I had Joe Welsh was playing drum. And he was the only... Him and, let's see, Cantrell, the only two drum players that really played drum by music. That's Joe Welsh and Cantrell. Louis Cantrell. He could take drum music and tune his drum by the music too. And he played any drum part. He was strictly a drummer by music, by notes. Well, them fellas could give me a whole lot of idea about, you know, reading and... So, when, after I got with Hippolyte Charles, I was playing tenor banjo then. Well, he, uh, different times when I had spare time. It'd give me an idea about the division and, you know, the treble clef. Well, then they were using orchestration parts. That time they had the orchestration. Music was different from what it is now. You had the introduction. It was third grade music, but you had the introduction down to the chord. And it stopped. Number one, number two, modulate. They modulate from different chords, different keys, changed keys, you see. They call that modulating down until... And then, uh, and then the repeat song go back and play that chorus until you go out. And then when you go out, you make the chord and go out, you see. So I found out how to read that good. And, uh, people I chose was strictly a music band. Uh, band, you had to know how to read music to play in it, man. Yeah, because he, uh, he had all, uh, men, uh, people in his band that could read, you see.
